summary: The note describes how Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are adopting Internet of Things (IoT) technology to modernize supply chain management. It uses case studies such as EverFresh Produce, Quantum Crafts, Global Textiles Inc. and EcoWare Packaging to show gains in waste reduction, delivery speed, customer satisfaction, resilience and sustainability. It also covers sensors, analytics and AI, collaborative platforms, and the challenges of investment, cybersecurity and training.
one_line: IoT is helping SMEs improve supply chain efficiency, resilience, customer transparency and sustainability, illustrated by several small-business case studies.
key_facts: Since September 2023, more SMEs have adopted IoT solutions because the technology became more accessible and cost-effective.
EverFresh Produce, a mid-sized organic fruit and vegetable supplier in Portland, Maine, adopted an IoT supply chain system in late 2023 and reduced waste by 30% and improved delivery times by 50%.
EverFresh Produce founder Johnathan Meyers said: "We were playing catch-up to demand surges and our waste levels were intolerable."
EverFresh Produce uses temperature-recording sensors in packaging that alert a central system if produce risks spoiling during transit.
Anita Rodriguez launched the IoT-driven logistics company TrackWise Solutions in January 2024, offering dynamic routing, inventory forecasting and predictive maintenance using machine learning.

Quantum Crafts, a custom furniture maker in Richmond, Virginia, launched an IoT order-tracking system in April 2024 that lets customers see order progress in real time, and CEO Marcus Washington said customer satisfaction scores have skyrocketed.

In November 2023, Global Textiles Inc. of Austin, Texas used IoT monitoring to notify customers and rearrange logistics when a container ship was delayed by bad weather, boosting client trust and loyalty.

In September 2024, a consortium of small businesses including EverFresh Produce and Quantum Crafts created a shared IoT platform called ChainLink Ecosystem, enabling collective bargaining with transport and logistics vendors.
Small Biz Tech, an innovation center founded by Rachel Thompson and launched in February 2025, offers SMEs resources, funding assistance and expertise for moving to IoT-based operations.
Key challenges for SMEs adopting IoT are technology investment, cybersecurity concerns and the need for employee training.
EcoWare Packaging, a sustainable packaging startup, uses IoT sensors to manage raw materials and achieved a 20% decrease in energy consumption as of its first quarter in 2025.
RFID tags provide instant information on an item's whereabouts, turning inventory management into a precise science.
